hard_case: Both tests pass exactly two items, so limiting the sum to two items changes nothing they can see.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: `let total: u32 = items.iter().copied().sum();` becomes `let total: u32 = items.iter().take(2).sum();`, and the test's inputs do not tell the two apart
not equivalent: `let total: u32 = items.iter().copied().sum();` becomes `let total: u32 = items.iter().map(|n| n * 2).sum();`

reasoning: `take(2)` equals the full sum for two items and survives; doubling each item gives total=60 and fails total_is_reported while the count test stays at two lines. Shape: input length never exceeds the window.
